text: The rapid development of metasurface has produced new possibilities for manipulating the sound waves with unprecedented precision and versatility. Leveraging advanced processing techniques such as 3-dimensional (3D) printing and nano-/micro-etching, various metasurface devices were implemented with remarkable capabilities in achieving the exceptional sound reflection and transmission. In biomedical engineering, successful applications of acoustic metasurface devices remain elusive due to many challenges such as impedance mismatching between instruments and issues, and the requirement of 2D fingerprint for integration and biocompatibility. Here, we propose a prototype of meta-skin-based ultrasonic instrument for applications of highly selective ultrasound neurostimulation and treatment. The meta-skin is flexible and biocompatible, with a thickness of only 20 μm (~ 1 / 15 of ultrasound wavelength at 5 MHz). The meta-skin can be further patterned into a meta-lens, which is sealed in hydrogel with a transducer. The meta-skin-based device can be seamlessly attached to tissues or skulls of animals with acoustic transparency and subwavelength-scale focusing (focal spot size ~220 μm). As an example, we utilized the meta-skin-based instrument to selectively stimulate sciatic nerves in rats. Moreover, the proposed device can make the focused ultrasound beam penetrate the skull and accurately stimulate small nucleus in target regions of the brain, which provides a potential therapeutic treatment for Parkinson’s disease.
